title: Drift-aware Gradual Upgrade Framework and Automated Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a drift-aware progressive delivery framework for runtime upgrades and model version promotions. Goals: minimize user-visible regressions, enforce LTS compatibility rules, reduce manual toil for canaries and rollbacks, and introduce automated fallback paths when runtime or model drift is detected. The scope covers: - version compatibility checks (binary, weights, KV cache schema) - staged traffic ramps with adaptive gates driven by telemetry - canary cohorts, shadowing and mirrored traffic modes - feature-flag driven opt-in/out and emergency kill-switch - automatic rollback policies tied to SLO/quality gates - tooling to declare LTS channels and safe upgrade windows
rollout_plan_summary: 1) Preflight: run compatibility checks and smoke-tests on preprod cluster; 2) Canary: route 0.5% traffic to canary cohort for 10 minutes with full tracing; 3) Adaptive ramp: increase to 5%, 20%, 50% using telemetry gates (latency p95, error rate, quality delta); 4) Final cutover: promote to LTS channel if all gates green; 5) Auto-rollback: trigger immediate fallback if any critical gate trips; 6) Post-mortem: automated artifact collection and release note generation.
gating_thresholds: Latency (p95): +20% relative to baseline triggers investigate; +40% -> rollback
Error rate (5xx or internal errors): >0.5% sustained over 5m -> rollback
Quality delta (eval prompt set): mean response similarity drop >2% -> rollback
Resource pressure (GPU mem/queue length): sustained >85% for 3m -> throttle and pause ramp
acceptance_criteria: Automated preflight compatibility checks run as part of release pipeline and block on failures
Adaptive ramp controller can progress a rollout using telemetry gates without manual intervention
Auto-rollback executes a safe, tested fallback (model or runtime) within 60s of trigger
Canary cohort telemetry surfaced in Console dashboards with per-route breakdowns
Feature flag exists to force-enable/disable progressive ramps per-customer and globally
Post-deploy artifacts (trace, logs, sample requests) are attached to the release for postmortem
